reasons.reproducibility: Whole-lake H2O2 dosing needs permits, boats and industrial dosing gear.
reasons.effectiveness: Cyanobacteria and microcystin fell 99% within days and stayed low for 7 weeks.
reasons.cost: Treating a whole lake at 2 mg/L costs far more than $5,000.
reasons.time: The 99% drop appeared within a few days (vitality fell within hours).
reasons.environment: H2O2 gone within days and most non-target groups largely unaffected, though 'largely' leaves minor harm possible.

reasons.reproducibility: Flask tests with cultivable kelp/Ulva against toxic Alexandrium are sponsor-doable; the 300 L mesocosm part is harder.
reasons.effectiveness: Kelp cut Alexandrium 73% in 48 h and Ulva 54% in 96 h in mesocosms, but flask results ranged 17-96%.
reasons.cost: Seaweed, toxic culture and saxitoxin assay about $150-500.
reasons.environment: Seaweed is retrievable, but Ulva pushed pH to 9-10 and other algae replaced the target.

reasons.reproducibility: Stocking 3.2 million clams across 64 plots in Shinnecock Bay is a multi-year field program.
reasons.effectiveness: Brown tide fell from 0.3-1.9e6 to <1e4 cells/mL, but the link is correlational with no controls.
reasons.cost: 3.2 M clams and field work far over $5,000.
reasons.environment: Clams are native and harvestable; clam densities rose 18x and chl a fell; no harm reported.

reasons.reproducibility: The typical reviewed use is field clay spraying at 4-10 t/km2 in China.
reasons.effectiveness: Modified clays remove HAB cells far better than natural clays, but no percent removal given in abstract.
reasons.environment: Clay settles to the seabed and is not retrieved (persistent material), despite authors' no-harm conclusion.

reasons.reproducibility: Field trial in a disused UK canal.
reasons.effectiveness: Reduced filamentous algae per summary, but no numbers or controls seen.
reasons.cost: Straw is cheap but canal-scale trial likely $500-5,000.
reasons.environment: Not reported; decaying straw adds organic matter.

reasons.reproducibility: Bench Microcystis with chlorine, ozone, KMnO4, CuSO4 and H2O2 needs an ozone generator and flow cytometry.
reasons.effectiveness: Chlorine compromised ≥88% of cells in 1 min and ozone 90% in 5 min, but only CuSO4 and H2O2 held over 7 days.
reasons.cost: Ozone generator and cell-integrity assays about $150-500.
reasons.environment: All oxidants lyse membranes and release toxins; CuSO4 arm adds metal.
